title: Louisiana Act 810 NIL Consent Checklist
tagline: What should be in writing before anyone uses a minor's name, image, or likeness in Louisiana.
description: A family-use checklist for Louisiana Act 810 NIL consent: who signs, what the written consent should cover, and what good records look like.
intro: Act 810 governs name, image, and likeness (NIL) rights in Louisiana. Before a minor's image appears in a highlight, a sponsorship post, or a clinic video, written consent needs to exist. This one-page checklist walks families through the decision points so consent is explicit, dated, and documented.
bullets: Who must sign: consent typically involves the parent or guardian and the minor
What the consent covers: the purpose of use, channels, duration, and any compensation terms
What records to keep: signed copies, dates, and the platform or use each consent applies to
When to revisit: after a transfer, a birthday, or a change in who controls the account
Education first: this checklist is guidance, not legal advice; a lawyer should review final documents whenever money is involved

title: Verify Your Would-Be Sports Agent
tagline: A simple pre-signing checklist for families and student-athletes.
description: How to verify someone who claims to be a sports agent before signing anything: registration, credentials, written terms, and red flags.
intro: Louisiana regulates athlete agents through the Representing Athletes Act (La. R.S. 51:2500 et seq.). Before a family signs any agreement, someone claiming to represent an athlete should be registered, verifiable, and willing to put every term in writing.
bullets: Confirm the person is a registered sports agent for your state, or an attorney in good standing
Ask who licenses or registers them and how to verify it - then verify it yourself
Get every scope, fee, and expense term in a signed written agreement
Do not sign under time pressure or before conflicts of interest are disclosed
An 'education, not representation' consultant should say so in writing and never hold themselves out as an agent
Red flags: guaranteed outcomes, cash-upfront demands, or eligibility treated as an afterthought

title: Master vs. Sync vs. Neighboring Rights
tagline: Three rights in one song - and who gets paid for each.
description: A one-page reference on the difference between a master recording, synchronization (sync), and neighboring rights in music.
intro: A single song contains multiple rights. In highlight reels, event content, and social video, schools and creators routinely need more than one permission. This reference untangles the three most common rights so the next clearance question is clear.
bullets: Master: the actual sound recording and who owns that file
Sync: the right to pair music with moving images - required for any video using a song
Neighboring rights: performance-side royalties tied to the recording, adjacent to copyright
Highlight reels usually need both master and sync clearance; buying the song does not grant sync rights
When in doubt, treat unlicensed music in video as a clearance question, not a taste question

title: Sample Brand & IP Audit: Redacted Findings
tagline: What families and schools receive - a redacted sample of the audit deliverable.
description: A redacted excerpt showing the structure of a media copyright and facility brand audit: current footprint, licensing risk, and next steps.
intro: One audit deliverable is a written findings document. This redacted sample shows the structure families and schools receive: current footprint, platform and licensing risk, and prioritized next steps. All identifying details are removed. It is a demonstration of form, not a promise of results.
bullets: Footprint: where the athlete, family, or school appears today
Risk review: platform terms (such as Hudl), music in video, and consent gaps
Prioritized actions: what to fix first, what to fix before signing anything
Evidence: the family or school keeps control of every asset and account throughout

title: Find a Producer: Launch Flyer
tagline: A one-page flyer for the upcoming producer directory.
description: A flyer explaining the Find a Producer directory: free browsing for artists, optional paid listings for producers, and the pre-launch interest list.
intro: Find a Producer is the pre-launch directory connecting artists and creative buyers with Louisiana producers. Browsing will be free; producers may purchase an optional listing after attorney review. Enrollment is not active yet - join the free interest list to be notified at launch.
bullets: Free to browse and contact listed producers once the directory opens
Optional paid listing for producers, activated only after attorney review
No representation and no music sales - business happens directly between producer and buyer
Join the free interest list from any page: the contact form at the bottom of the home page
